svg.title: Pre-War European Jewish Life: 9.5 Million Lives & Diversity (c. 1933)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 9 historical GIS choropleth atlas map of interwar Europe (c. 1933) showing pre-Anschluss national boundaries and pre-war Jewish population distribution across Poland (~3.3 million), the Western Soviet Union (~2.5 million), Greater Romania (~756,000), Hungary (~445,000), Czechoslovakia (~357,000), Germany (~525,000), Western Europe, and the Sephardic community of Salonica, Greece (~55,000).

g.text: Major Pre-War Jewish Cultural & Civic Centre

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: THE SHOAH
Pre-War European Jewish Life: 9.5 Million Lives & Diversity (c. 1933)
Before 1939, ~9.5 million Jewish people enriched every part of Europe—from Yiddish-speaking Poland & USSR to Salonica’s Sephardic port.
In Germany, Jews were under 1% of the population and deeply integrated citizens; in Eastern Europe lived over half of European Jewry.
